page: Microsoft Azure EC2es_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on x86_64 Intel Xeon TDX processors running under Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 2 vCPUs backed by 1 dedicated physical core with 2 threads per core, operating at clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB, providing an elevated 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include an expansive 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance does not include dedicated GPUs or local ephemeral storage, requiring remote or managed block storage for persistent data.

Benchmark data reflects strong single-thread execution paired with limited aggregate throughput due to the low core count. In Geekbench testing, the instance achieved a single-core score of 1943.0, placing it in the top 25 percent of tested machines. Conversely, multi-core metrics fall into lower percentiles, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2182.0 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 1962.27 placing in the bottom 10 to 25 percent. Highly parallel tasks such as Clang compilation and ray tracing demonstrate constrained performance due to the two-thread ceiling, while Redis SET performance registers at 2.58 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the EC2es_v6 delivers a dense memory-to-vCPU ratio without forcing provisioning of excess compute cores. It functions well for single-threaded or low-concurrency workloads that need moderate memory capacity, such as in-memory caches, small relational database instances, background message workers, and lightweight analytical jobs that benefit from modern Intel vector and matrix extensions.
